sn22.100:2.1: Said by the commentary to be a large painting taken from place to place by certain brahmin heretics in their “wanderings” and exhibited to illustrate kamma and its results. This suggests the sense of “conduct” (_caraṇa_), but the commentary does not make this connection. Also, the commentary says the brahmins were of the Sāṁkhya school, but this is anachronistic as that school arose much later.
sn22.100:2.3: The text plays on three homonyms of _citta_: “mind”, “painting”, and “elaborate”.
